themes_detail.label: Dangling Street Signs Safety Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Street sign-related complaints spiked to 10 reports THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 2.4 per week (UP 321%), suggesting a sudden infrastructure hazard affecting pedestrian and vehicular safety in Queens Village/Cambria Heights.
evidence: 10 Street Sign - Dangling complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.41)
321% increase from baseline, classified as high-severity statistical anomaly
Spike is acute and immediate, not gradual
reporting_angles: Physical audit of street signage across major intersections to document hazards and investigate root cause (weather event, maintenance backlog, contractor issues)
Interview DOT about signage inspection cycles and whether recent storms or other events triggered the spike

themes_detail.label: Curb Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped to 5 reports THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.6 per week (UP 700%), indicating rapid street infrastructure degradation that could affect vehicle access and pedestrian mobility.
evidence: 5 Curb Condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.29)
700% increase from baseline, classified as high-severity statistical anomaly
Correlates with 2,002 Street Condition complaints over 90 days (highest volume category), suggesting systemic maintenance issues
reporting_angles: Document specific curb damage locations and photograph deterioration patterns to establish whether this is localized or district-wide
Investigate whether recent weather, heavy vehicle traffic, or deferred maintenance is responsible; compare to DOT repair queue timelines

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials Spike
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints surged to 4 reports last week, an 8-fold jump from the 0.5 weekly baseline (UP 700%), suggesting potential environmental or industrial contamination concerns requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 4 Hazardous Materials complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.95)
700% increase from baseline, classified as high-severity statistical anomaly
Related spike: Illegal Tree Damage UP 380% (3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 avg), possibly indicating contamination or industrial activity damage
reporting_angles: FOIL 311 complaint details to identify specific hazmat types and locations; cross-reference with EPA/DEC industrial site databases and recent spills

Interview NYCDEP and local residents about potential contamination sources (industrial facilities, illegal dumping, transit/logistics hubs); note active JFK Conduit Logistics Center demapping (completed ULURP) may be relevant

themes_detail.label: Illegal Cannabis Retail Growth
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints jumped to 9 reports last week from a baseline of 2.5 per week (UP 260%), indicating rapid expansion of unlicensed cannabis operations in the district.
evidence: 9 Cannabis Retailer complaints last week vs. 2.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.11)
260% increase from baseline, classified as high-severity statistical anomaly
Reflects statewide proliferation of unlicensed operators exploiting gaps between state legalization and NYC enforcement
reporting_angles: Map the 9 reported illegal retailers from last week; identify whether they're clustered in specific neighborhoods or dispersed; assess proximity to schools/youth centers
Interview NYPD, OCME (Office of Cannabis Management), and local residents about enforcement challenges; determine whether the surge reflects new store openings or increased complaint reporting

themes_detail.label: Deteriorating Building Conditions
themes_detail.summary: Flooring/stairs complaints spiked to 8 reports 3 weeks ago (UP 357% from 1.8 baseline), and 695 building permits filed in the last 90 days suggest significant construction/renovation activity potentially masking or causing interior housing defects.
evidence: 8 Flooring/Stairs complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.49)
357% increase from baseline, classified as high-severity statistical anomaly
695 total DOB permits filed in last 90 days (470 alterations + 81 alteration COs) suggest renovation-driven disruption and potential code violations
reporting_angles: Sample complaints to identify whether flooring/stairs issues are post-renovation defects, deferred maintenance in older buildings, or structural concerns; cross-reference complaint addresses with active DOB permits
Interview tenants and landlords about renovation quality and code compliance; investigate whether permit approval/inspection timelines are adequate
